question: What is the main difference between acquired and congenital immune deficiencies?

options.A: Congenital deficiencies only affect the T-cells
options.B: Acquired deficiencies develop later in life due to outside factors
options.C: Congenital deficiencies always show clear signs in adulthood
options.D: Acquired deficiencies are permanent and can never change

explanation: Acquired immune deficiencies happen because of outside environmental or health factors after a person has had a normally working immune system. [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h1)

question: Why are patients with weak immune systems in big danger from everyday germs?

options.A: Their weak immune system cannot control harmless organisms
options.B: Their bodies make poisons that attract common bacteria
options.C: Their red blood cell count drops and starves tissues
options.D: Their skin lets airborne spores pass straight through

explanation: Opportunistic germs take advantage of a body's low defenses to cause serious illness when the immune system is compromised. [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h1)

question: Which specific cells are mainly attacked as HIV infection gets worse?

options.D: White blood cells that fight clotting

explanation: The human immunodeficiency virus specifically attaches to surface receptors on CD4+ T-cells, which eventually destroys them. [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h2)

question: What happens directly when the body loses T-helper cell function?

options.B: Bone marrow stops making new blood cells completely
options.C: Red blood cells multiply too fast and thicken the blood
options.D: The body loses coordination of its overall immune response

explanation: T-helper cells act like master coordinators that signal other immune cells to fight infections properly. [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h2)

question: At what CD4 cell count does an HIV infection officially progress to AIDS?
explanation: When T-helper cells drop below the 200 count threshold, the body's cellular immunity becomes too weak, meeting the definition for AIDS. [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h3)

question: An HIV-positive patient shows no symptoms for several years. What is this phase called?
explanation: During the clinical latency or chronic asymptomatic phase, the virus multiplies at low levels without causing obvious signs of illness. [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h3)

question: How does severe malnutrition directly weaken the body's immune defenses?

options.A: It lacks the amino acids needed to build antibodies and immune cells
options.B: It forces the liver to destroy healthy white blood cells
options.C: It blocks the lymphatic vessels completely
options.D: It stops stomach acid from working and kills good gut bacteria

explanation: A lack of protein in the diet starves the body of the building blocks it needs to make new immune cells and proteins. [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h4)

question: Which common childhood illness can cause temporary immune amnesia?
explanation: The measles virus attacks memory cells in the immune system, wiping out protection against other diseases the body had previously learned to fight. [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h4)

question: What is a major medical treatment cause of bone marrow suppression during cancer care?
explanation: Chemotherapy medicines kill fast-dividing cells in the bone marrow, which causes a sharp drop in white blood cell counts. [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h5)

question: Why do organ transplant patients need ongoing care to suppress their immune systems?

options.A: To keep normal bacteria from turning into cancer cells
options.B: To stop them from developing severe iron deficiency anemia
options.C: To help surgical wounds close up faster
options.D: To stop their body from rejecting the new organ

explanation: Doctors purposefully prescribe immunosuppressive drugs to keep the patient's natural defenses from attacking the new transplant tissue. [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h5)

question: Which diagnostic test counts the exact number of T-helper cells in a patient's blood?
explanation: A CD4 test measures and counts the specific helper T-cells circulating in a blood sample. [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h6)

question: A patient comes in with white patches in the mouth and a long-lasting fever. What health issue should a nurse think of first?
explanation: Oral thrush and ongoing fevers are classic signs that a patient's immune system is failing and struggling to protect them. [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h6)

question: What is the main reason healthcare workers must wash their hands carefully around patients with weak immune systems?

options.A: To remove natural skin oils that protect against fungi
options.B: To keep the patient from sweating on medical tools
options.C: To stop hospital germs from spreading to a vulnerable patient
options.D: To help blood flow better in small skin vessels

explanation: Good hand hygiene stops nurses and visitors from carrying environmental germs onto patients who cannot fight them off. [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h7)

question: Which food safety rule is most important for a patient with a very weak immune system?

options.B: Avoid raw or unpasteurized food products completely
options.C: Eat plenty of raw, unwashed green leafy vegetables

explanation: Raw foods often carry bacteria and parasites that a weak immune system cannot handle, which leads to dangerous infections. [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h7)

question: What does PMTCT stand for in public health programs?

options.A: Program for Malaria and Tuberculosis Control
options.B: Primary Medical Treatment for Chronic Trauma

explanation: PMTCT programs use medical steps to stop infections from passing from pregnant mothers to their babies. [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h8)

question: Why are community health nurses so important in managing immune deficiencies in Nigeria?

options.A: They manufacture antiretroviral drugs inside rural clinics
options.B: They help reduce stigma and improve access to local testing and treatment
options.C: They enforce mandatory quarantine laws for families
options.D: They take the place of laboratories by doing physical exams

explanation: Community nurses bridge the gap between hospitals and local towns, helping people feel accepted so they will stick to their treatments. [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h8)
